name: Harmonious Graph
description: You're given an undirected graph with $$$n$$$ nodes and $$$m$$$ edges. Nodes are numbered from $$$1$$$ to $$$n$$$. The graph is considered harmonious if and only if the following property holds: For every triple of integers $$$(l, m, r)$$$ such that $$$1 \le l \lt m \lt r \le n$$$, if there exists a path going from node $$$l$$$ to node $$$r$$$, then there exists a path going from node $$$l$$$ to node $$$m$$$. In other words, in a harmonious graph, if from a node $$$l$$$ we can reach a node $$$r$$$ through edges ($$$l \lt r$$$), then we should able to reach nodes $$$(l+1), (l+2), \ldots, (r-1)$$$ too. What is the minimum number of edges we need to add to make the graph harmonious?
input_specification: The first line contains two integers $$$n$$$ and $$$m$$$ ($$$3 \le n \le 200\ 000$$$ and $$$1 \le m \le 200\ 000$$$). The $$$i$$$-th of the next $$$m$$$ lines contains two integers $$$u_i$$$ and $$$v_i$$$ ($$$1 \le u_i, v_i \le n$$$, $$$u_i \neq v_i$$$), that mean that there's an edge between nodes $$$u$$$ and $$$v$$$. It is guaranteed that the given graph is simple (there is no self-loop, and there is at most one edge between every pair of nodes).
output_specification: Print the minimum number of edges we have to add to the graph to make it harmonious.
approach_summary: Maintain disjoint sets using path compression and union by rank/size. Process edge additions and component queries in O(α(N)) amortized time.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1253D — Harmonious Graph [80. DSU / Union Find]
topic_editorial.key_invariant: Connectivity is an equivalence relation. By organizing connected components into trees and merging smaller trees into larger ones (`union-by-rank/size`) combined with path compression, find and union operations run in near-constant inverse Ackermann time $O(\alpha(N))$.
